clue.text: A sporty sort detains dreadful old woman philosopher

indicators.note: to detain is to hold someone in, so the scrambled letters close round the other piece
to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of the two words before it are shuffled

parts.note: a hag is an ugly, frightening old woman

explanation.surface: An athletic type holds on to a fearsome crone who happens to be a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' reads as a noun ('a sporty sort') but rearranges A SPORTY into PYTORAS; 'detains' then puts HAG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker famous for the theorem on right-angled triangles was a philosopher and mathematician.

clue.text: Leave car for explorer-author

definitions.meaning: to leave a vehicle standing in a place
Mungo ..., Scottish explorer who wrote up his travels

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave a vehicle for a travel writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a car somewhere is to park it; Mungo Park was the Scottish explorer of the Niger who wrote Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa.

clue.text: Last best heart in Steele publication gossip

indicators.note: something put at the heart of a word goes into its middle

parts.note: Richard Steele founded the periodical The Tatler in 1709

indicators.note: the last of 'best' means only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A tip-off about the best final piece of gossip from Steele's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'best', T, goes into the middle of TATLER, Steele's paper, giving the double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a person who chatters idly and spreads rumours, a gossip.

clue.text: Kind of a deal sought by Forster's girl

indicators.note: a kind of something is a version of it, so the letters of 'a deal' are rearranged

parts.note: to have sought something is to have quested for it

explanation.surface: A girl in Forster looks for a certain sort of bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of a deal' reads as a type of bargain, but 'Kind of' rearranges A DEAL into ADELA.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Englishwoman at the centre of A Passage to India, whose accusation drives the plot, is Forster's heroine.

clue.text: Royal birds featured in such a gift from Buck Mulligan

definitions.text: Royal birds featured in such a gift from Buck Mulligan

parts.words: Royal birds featured in such a gift from Buck Mulligan
parts.note: swans are the royal birds; Oliver St John Gogarty, the model for Joyce's Buck Mulligan, gave swans to the Liffey and named a book of poems after such a present of swans

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of present Joyce's mocking medical student gave, involving royal birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Swans in England belong to the Crown, hence 'Royal birds'. Gogarty's poems were titled An Offering of Swans, after the birds he presented to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift presented, especially as a token or tribute, is an offering.

clue.text: Direction taken by riparian Hemingway and Benson

definitions.text: Direction taken by riparian Hemingway and Benson

parts.words: Direction taken by riparian Hemingway and Benson
parts.note: riparian means by a riverbank: a Hemingway title has a man passing over a river into the trees, and an E. F. Benson title has him passing over a stream; the shared first word of both names a way to travel

explanation.surface: Which way two writers went when beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The titles are Hemingway's novel about a river and the trees and Benson's novel about a stream; both begin with the same preposition, which is also one of the two directions of a crossword entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword entries run one of two ways, down or the other one; here it is the horizontal direction.

clue.text: Put up with Antigonus's pursuer

definitions.meaning: in The Winter's Tale Antigonus leaves the stage 'pursued by' an animal, the most famous stage direction in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Tolerating the one who chased a Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to bear something; Antigonus exits chased by a bear in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Lioness in winter?

parts.note: the play and film The Lion in Winter has Henry II as the lion; the female counterpart is his queen

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the twist on the title The Lion in Winter: the lioness is the lion's wife, the queen of Aquitaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine is Henry II's queen in The Lion in Winter, so she is the female of the title's lion.

clue.text: Hope hero destroyed sly slander

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the letters of 'sly slander' are rearranged

explanation.surface: The hero brought down by a sneaky smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' looks like the everyday word, but it is Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Rassendyll is the Englishman who impersonates the King of Ruritania in Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda, its hero.

clue.text: Physicist, and groove vehicle got into her

indicators.note: the two pieces are entered with the pronoun placed between them, inside the pair

parts.note: a rut is a groove worn in a track
a Ford is a make of car, so a vehicle

explanation.surface: A scientist, a rut and a car somehow involved with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into' looks like it sends the car into 'her', but here the pronoun sits inside the pair of synonyms. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Rutherford, the New Zealand-born scientist who split the atom, was a physicist.

clue.text: God backs up canal

indicators.note: to back up is to go backwards, so the canal's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A deity supports a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs up' looks like 'supports', but it reverses SUEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of the Olympian gods in Greek myth is a god.

clue.text: Mamet's depraved character with poet's hero from Dumas

parts.note: David Mamet's play Edmond follows a man's descent into depravity
belonging to Dante, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: A playwright's corrupt figure joins a poet's hero in a French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces. The possessive 's of 'poet's' gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor wrongly imprisoned who becomes the Count of Monte Cristo is the protagonist of Dumas's novel.

clue.text: Transparent-sounding Durrell protagonist

indicators.note: '-sounding' means the word for transparent is said out loud, not spelt

parts.note: transparent means ..., as glass is

explanation.surface: A Durrell character who seems to be see-through.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R of 'clear' is silent, so it is said like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clea Montis is the painter who gives her name to the last novel of Durrell's Alexandria Quartet.

clue.text: Neruda's dwelling here below

parts.note: Pablo Neruda's collection Residencia en la tierra is titled in English as an abode on Earth; 'here below' means on earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'here below' is an old phrase for this world, standing for 'on Earth' in Neruda's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a home, a place where one lives; the clue nods to the title of Neruda's poems.

clue.text: "It's significant", we hear but in fact it's superficial knowledge

indicators.note: this tells us the phrase is spoken aloud, slurred together

parts.note: if something is significant, it's mattering

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a thing is important, when really they know only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's mattering' said quickly drops the opening 'it', leaving 's mattering', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, shallow acquaintance with a subject is a smattering.

clue.text: Blemish when French novelist reaches point of no return

definitions.text: novelist reaches point of no return

parts.note: to blemish is to mar
quand is the French word for 'when'

explanation.surface: A flaw appears at the moment a writer passes the stage where he cannot turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' goes with 'when', not 'novelist': Marquand was American, and Point of No Return is one of his novels.
explanation.definitionFit: John P. Marquand, the American writer, published the novel Point of No Return in 1949.

clue.text: Byron's corsair told tales of the sea

definitions.meaning: the pirate hero of Byron's poem The Corsair
Joseph ..., the Polish-born novelist of the sea

explanation.surface: Byron's pirate spinning yarns about his voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's poem The Corsair has a pirate captain of that name, and Joseph Conrad wrote sea stories such as Lord Jim and Typhoon.

clue.text: Hair came — completely new production — it was fabulous!

indicators.note: a completely new production remakes the material, so the letters of 'Hair came' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre review: the musical Hair returned in a brand-new staging, and it was wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair' suggests the musical and 'fabulous' praise, but 'fabulous' means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, lion, goat and serpent in one, is a creature of fable.

clue.text: Bennett's st, of st.?

parts.note: Arnold Bennett wrote a novel whose title is a saint's name followed by 'of' and the name of a Roman road ending in Street; 'st' abbreviates both saint and street

explanation.walkthrough: The two 'st's stand first for Saint (St Teresa of Avila) and then for Street: Watling Street is an old Roman road in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa of Watling Street is Arnold Bennett's 1904 novel, and Teresa is the name of a famous saint.

clue.text: Novelist noted for his careful brushwork

definitions.meaning: Frederic ..., author of The Glittering Prizes
the Italian Renaissance painter of the School of Athens

explanation.surface: A writer famed for meticulous painting technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Raphael is a novelist and screenwriter, and Raphael of Urbino was a High Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Virtuoso Laureate

definitions.meaning: The Virtuoso is a 1676 comedy by Thomas ...
Thomas ... was made Poet Laureate in 1689

explanation.surface: A brilliant performer who also holds the poet's office.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Shadwell wrote the comedy The Virtuoso and succeeded Dryden as Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Improved by instruction and, with a slip of a pen, made an Olympian

indicators.text: with a slip of a pen
indicators.note: a slip of the pen misplaces a letter, so one letter of the word is shifted to a new spot

parts.note: to make someone one of the gods of Olympus is to deify them

explanation.surface: Someone improved by teaching, and by a miswriting turned into a god.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening D of DEIFIED moves one place right, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to improve someone morally or intellectually by teaching.

clue.text: Conciliate the Venus de Milo, for example?

definitions.text: the Venus de Milo, for example?
definitions.meaning: the famous statue has lost both its arms

explanation.surface: Placate the armless statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the statue has been 'dis-armed', relieved of its arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone over and allay hostility is to disarm them; a statue whose arms are lost has been literally deprived of them.

clue.text: "The inflated style is itself a kind of —" (Orwell)

definitions.text: "The inflated style is itself a kind of —" (Orwell)

parts.words: "The inflated style is itself a kind of —" (Orwell)
parts.note: a line from Orwell's essay Politics and the English Language, where the missing word is a mild expression standing in for a blunt one

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the term for a gentle phrase used instead of a blunt one.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell argued that inflated prose softens and disguises its meaning, as a polite substitute for a harsh word does.

clue.text: French friends of well-known pére et fils?

definitions.meaning: Kingsley ... and his son Martin, both novelists

explanation.surface: A French father and son known as pals.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural for 'friend' is amis, and Kingsley and Martin are the famous father-and-son novelists of that surname.

clue.text: Prince seeks alternatives in Ring hoard

indicators.note: alternate letters of the words that follow, taking every other one

explanation.surface: A prince hunts for treasure in Wagner's Ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring hoard' suggests Wagner's gold, but the every-other letters of RING HOARD are taken: rIng hOaRd. 'seeks' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Borodin's opera Prince Igor is about the medieval Russian ruler of that name.

clue.text: Indian costume unusually worn by Egyptian lady-in-waiting

indicators.note: a garment worn in an unusual way is rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: a sari is the draped garment worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: An Indian dress worn oddly by a maid of an Egyptian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually worn' rearranges SARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: 24 subject is privy object?

parts.note: jakes is an old word for a lavatory, a privy
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A father-and-son subject turns out to be a toilet item.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' refers to AMIS: Jake's Thing is a 1978 novel by Kingsley Amis. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis's comic novel about a man's lost libido is one of his books, a subject of the Amis entry.

clue.text: It's mine, wrote Wilbur Smith, with another bestseller

definitions.text: It's mine, wrote Wilbur Smith, with another bestseller

parts.words: It's mine, wrote Wilbur Smith, with another bestseller
parts.note: Wilbur Smith's novels include ... Mine, so the word before 'mine' in that title is wanted; it is also the title of another of his books

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's mine' reads as a claim of ownership but means the word placed before 'Mine' in a title.
explanation.definitionFit: The precious yellow metal names Wilbur Smith's Gold Mine and his novel Gold, so it fits both titles.

clue.text: James's envoy

parts.note: Henry James's novel The ... is about Lambert Strether sent to Paris as an emissary

explanation.walkthrough: James is Henry James, author of The Ambassadors; the clue uses the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic representative, and Henry James titled a novel after such representatives.
